capitals.name: Imak (Imakia)
capitals.note: The page: Imak, 'near modern Pavlodar', was the khakan's summer seat; the years are the page's infobox span (880-1035) because the page dates nothing else. Coordinates are the gazetteer's Pavlodar, a placeholder; the gazetteer lacks Imak.

capitals.name: Tamim
capitals.note: The page: Tamim, 'on the southern shore of Lake Balkhash', was the winter capital. Placeholder point on that shore; the gazetteer lacks Tamim and the page gives no coordinates. After 1035 no page names a seat of the Kipchaks or Cumans, so no capital is drawn.

correction.text: years only: no Kimek state before 880; the Kimaks of 743-879 are a people on the Irtysh, partly under the Uyghur Khaganate, and the land is nobody's (grey)

keyframe_review.note: 750-792, 1.43 M km2 (51.3-84.8 E, 43.9-53.8 N). The Kimek-Kipchak page dates the state to 880 (infobox '880-1035'; 'End of the 9th to early 10th century: The Kimek state formed, ruled by a khagan'). For 743-879 it has only a people: 'the main body of the Kimaks remained in the Irtysh area', some stayed in the Uyghur Khaganate, part moved 'northwest to the Urals and southwest to Zhetysu' in the late 8th or early 9th century, and the bulk 'migrated to present-day Kazakhstan' after 840. No state, border or area is given for these years, so the shape is not used. Cliopatria's Qarlugs row (793-849) takes 129 of its cells in 793. The page gives no area to compare.

correction.text: years only: no Kimek state before 880

keyframe_review.note: 793-849, 1.42 M km2: the 750 shape with 129 cells in Semirechye given to the Qarlugs row and 112 added in the Altai. Not used for the same reason (state formed c. 880).

correction.text: years only: no Kimek state before 880

keyframe_review.note: 850-879, 1.43 M km2: the 793 shape plus 26 cells at 80.7-83.7 E. Not used: the page has the Kimaks move west and take Pecheneg lands on the Syr Darya and in the Aral area 'in the second half of the 9th century', but the state is formed only at its end (infobox 880).

880-895, 1.43 M km2 (Irtysh, Altai edge, Kazakh steppe, Urals edge and Aral steppe). The infobox starts the state in 880; the page puts the Kimaks on the Irtysh, in the Urals and Zhetysu and, from the second half of the 9th century, on the Syr Darya and in the Aral area. The page gives no area (no infobox figure to compare); the shape stands as the best draw of a soft steppe frontier.

896-969, 1.43 M km2: 100 cells added in the Ural-Turgay steppe (47.0-51.4 N, 51.3-63.8 E). Pecheneg page: 'Driven further west by the Khazars and Cumans by 889', 'drove the Magyars west of the Dnieper River by 892'; Kimek page: the Kimaks 'took Pecheneg lands along the Syr Darya and in the Aral area, and pushed the Pechenegs toward the Lower Volga'. The date 896 is Cliopatria's.
970-989: three cells drop out at the northern edge; unverified: page silent on this step (Cliopatria noise).
990-999: one cell drops out near the Syr Darya (67.9 E); unverified: page silent on this step.
1000-1045: a one-cell change (69.6-70.6 E); unverified: page silent on this step.

1046-1055, 1.46 M km2: a one-cell change; unverified: page silent. The infobox ends the confederation in 1035; the Cumans page has the first Rus' contact in 1055 ('The Cumans first encountered the Rus' in 1055'), so the row is kept as one continuing confederation under its later names.

1056-1065, 2.23 M km2: 2,783 cells added, 1,424 of them the whole Oghuz Turks shape (the Oghuz Yabgu State ends in 1055) and 1,359 the Volga-Don-Donets steppe west to 38.0 E. Kimek page: 'The Rus chronicles under the year 1054 record an appearance near Kyiv of the Oguz people', pushed by Kipchaks; Cumans page: 'The Cumans first encountered the Rus' in 1055'; Pecheneg page: after 1036 'other nomadic peoples replaced the weakened Pechenegs in the Pontic steppe', the Cumans and Torks. The Cumans page puts the confederation 'from the Danube in the west to Taraz, Kazakhstan in the east' (c. 1200); the shape stops at 38 E (see notes: Cliopatria's Halych-Volhynia occupation row holds the steppe west of it).
1066-1071: unchanged. Cumans page: 'at the Battle of the Alta River, they defeated the armies of three sons of Yaroslav the Wise' (1068), which moved no border on the page.

1072-1084, 3.02 M km2: 2,952 cells added in the south Urals, Bashkortostan and the Middle Volga (48.4-56.4 N, 38.3-70.9 E). The page describes the 12th-century territory as including 'the southern Urals, the eastern Volga, Mangyshlak, and the area northwest of the Aral Sea' but dates no step; the year 1072 is Cliopatria's (ledger gain, confidence 1).
1085-1093: unchanged. Cumans page: devastated Byzantine settlements in 1086, beaten by Ladislaus I in 1089, invaded eastern Hungary in 1091; none changes the shape.

region.text: the Kimek lands from the Irtysh to the Urals and the Aral steppe

ledger.note: 880: the Kimek khaganate forms on the Irtysh and the steppe to the west. Infobox '880-1035'; 'End of the 9th to early 10th century: The Kimek state formed, ruled by a khagan'. The page gives no border; the region is Cliopatria's 880 shape (Irtysh to the Urals and the Aral steppe), which fits its list of places.

region.text: the steppe north of the Aral Sea between the Ural River and the Turgay, vacated by the Pechenegs

ledger.note: 896: the Kimeks hold the Ural-Turgay steppe the Pechenegs had left. 'The Kimaks moved west, took Pecheneg lands along the Syr Darya and in the Aral area, and pushed the Pechenegs toward the Lower Volga' (second half of the 9th century); Pecheneg page: driven west 'by 889', 'west of the Dnieper River by 892'. The year 896 is Cliopatria's step, so confidence is 1.

1055: the Kipchaks, called Cumans in the west, meet the Rus'. 'The Cumans first encountered the Rus' in 1055.' The Kimek page's infobox ends the Kimek-Kipchak confederation in 1035 and has the Kipchaks 'independent within the Kaganate' and migrating west from the 10th century; Cliopatria keeps one row, so the confederation continues here under its Kipchak-Cuman names (confidence 1: the pages do not call it a renaming).

region.text: the Oghuz lands between the Caspian and Aral seas and along the Syr Darya

ledger.note: 1056: the Kipchaks take the Oghuz lands. 'The Rus chronicles under the year 1054 record an appearance near Kyiv of the Oguz people', pushed by Kipchaks; the Oghuz Yabgu State page: 'Kipchak pressure split the Oghuz' and 'Kimeks and Kipchaks ended the state'. Cliopatria's Kimek shape of 1056 holds 1,424 of the 1,425 Oghuz cells.

region.text: the steppe between the Volga, the Don and the Donets that the Pechenegs and Torks held

ledger.note: 1056: the Cumans reach the Pontic steppe east of the Don. 'The Cumans first encountered the Rus' in 1055.' Pecheneg page: after 1036 'other nomadic peoples replaced the weakened Pechenegs in the Pontic steppe', the Cumans and Torks, with no year. The 1,359 cells are the Volga-Don-Donets steppe west to 38 E; the date is Cliopatria's and the page's contact year.

region.text: the southern Urals, Bashkortostan and the eastern and middle Volga

ledger.note: 1072: the Kipchak lands reach the south Urals and the Middle Volga. The page describes the 12th-century territory as including 'the southern Urals, the eastern Volga, Mangyshlak, and the area northwest of the Aral Sea' but dates nothing; 1072 is Cliopatria's step.

union.text: the lower Syr Darya at Jand

region.text: Mangyshlak and the lower Syr Darya at Jand

ledger.note: 1138: Mangyshlak and the lower Syr Darya pass to Atsiz of Khwarazm. Atsiz page: 'In 1138, he rebelled openly against his suzerain' ... he 'conquered the Mangyshlak and lower bank of the Syr Darya, but was defeated in Hazarasp and forced to flee'; its closing section says he continued the land-gathering policy 'annexing Jand and Mangyshlak to Khwarazm'. The Atsiz page names no former holder; the Kimek page puts the Mangyshlak Peninsula in the confederation's territory in the 12th century (undated), so Kimek is taken as the holder before 1138 (as in the khwarezmid-dynasty gain of the same year). Added in fx-04 to match that gain; before it the Kimek shapes of 1139 and 1147 kept drawing the land.

region.text: the middle Syr Darya from Jend toward Otrar

ledger.note: 1147: the middle Syr Darya passes to the Qara Khitai. Cliopatria's Kara-Khitans row holds the 292 cells from 1147. The Qara Khitai page dates 'In 1137, he defeated the Western Karakhanids near Khujand and annexed Fergana and Tashkent' and the Battle of Qatwan (9 September 1141) but names no Kipchak land.

region.text: the lower Syr Darya below Jend

ledger.note: 1210: the lower Syr Darya passes to Khwarezm. Cliopatria's Khwarezmid Empire row holds 48 of the 49 cells from 1210. The Khwarazmian Empire page says nothing dated about the Kipchak steppe (Terken Khatun was a Qipchaq princess and Tekish had ties with Qipchak tribes near the Aral Sea, both undated).

region.text: the Irtysh and the Altai edge

ledger.note: 1220: the Irtysh and Altai go to the Mongols. 'Jochi (d. 1225) was given the lands (an ulus) around the Irtysh River' (undated); Cliopatria's Mongol Empire shape of 1220 holds 798 of the 804 cells. The Mongol invasion page has Subutai pursue the Merkit and Qangli Kipchak allies in northern Kazakhstan in 1217 or 1218 but return 'without incorporating' them.

region.text: the Kazakh steppe, the Aral steppe and the Urals

ledger.note: 1227: the Kazakh steppe, the Aral and the Urals pass to the Ulus of Jochi. Golden Horde infobox 'Established: c. 1225'. All 4,901 cells lie in Cliopatria's Mongol Empire shape of 1227; the Mongol invasion page puts the defeat of 'the eastern portions of Cumania' in 1236, so the page and the shape differ by about a decade. [fx-04, 2026-11-01] Counterpart re-pointed from mongol-empire to ulus-of-jochi: the Kimek page says 'The Mongols conquered the remnant of the Kimak Khanate, and its lands were assigned to the Ulus of Jochi' (13th century, undated), and with the Mongol Empire as counterpart the cells sat with it until the ulus's 1236 keyframe pulled them back. The Golden Horde page has Jochi's ulus 'around the Irtysh River', says 'Jochi died before he could significantly expand it' and has the kurultai of 1229 decide 'to subdue the Kipchaks', so no page dates the handover; 1227 stays Cliopatria's step (confidence 1). Mirror: ulus-of-jochi ledger gain 1227.

region.text: the Volga-Don steppe west of the Urals that remained

ledger.note: 1236: Batu's armies attack the western Cuman steppe. 'In 1236, the Mongols defeated the eastern portions of Cumania and swept into Eastern Europe.' The Golden Horde page: 'In 1235, Batu with the great general Subutai began an invasion westwards' and Volga Bulgaria fell in 1236.

region.text: the Volga-Don steppe west of the Urals that remained

ledger.note: 1241: Köten is murdered in Pest and Cuman control of the Pontic steppes ends. 'Köten was assassinated in Pest on 17 March 1241. Cuman control of the Pontic steppes ended in 1241, and the confederation ceased to exist.'

region.text: the Volga-Don steppe west of the Urals that remained

ledger.note: 1241: the Cuman steppe passes to the Ulus of Jochi. The Kimek page: 'The Mongols conquered the remnant of the Kimak Khanate, and its lands were assigned to the Ulus of Jochi' (13th century, undated); the Cumans page dates the end of Cuman control to 1241. [fx-04, 2026-11-01] Counterpart re-pointed from mongol-empire to ulus-of-jochi, as this note already reads: the Kimek page says its lands 'were assigned to the Ulus of Jochi'; the Cumans page has the Cuman-Kipchaks become subjects 'as part of what was to be known as the Golden Horde'. Mirror: ulus-of-jochi ledger gain 1241.

region.text: the Volga-Don steppe west of the Urals that remained

ledger.note: 1241: the Cuman-Kipchak confederation ceases to exist. 'Cuman control of the Pontic steppes ended in 1241, and the confederation ceased to exist.' Cliopatria ends its row in 1235. [fx-04, 2026-11-01] Counterpart ulus-of-jochi (see the 1241 loss and identity.successors).

wars.name: Kimek-Pecheneg wars

zones.text: the Aral steppes and the Syr Darya

wars.outcome: The Kimaks take Pecheneg lands on the Syr Darya and in the Aral area and push the Pechenegs toward the Lower Volga (second half of the 9th century).
wars.note: Years are the page's 'second half of the 9th century' rounded to the state's founding; no battle is dated.

wars.name: Rus'-Cuman wars
wars.outcome: A war 'lasting 175 years' from the 1061 Cuman invasion of Pereyaslavl: the Cumans beat three sons of Yaroslav at the Alta River (1068), Vladimir Monomakh at the Stugna (1093), were beaten near Lubny (1107), sacked six cities (1177), lost Khan Kobiak (1183) and beat Igor's campaign (1185). No border moved; raids on the steppe edge.
wars.note: Cumans page: 'In 1061, however, the Cumans, under the chieftain Sokal, invaded and devastated the Pereyaslavl principality.'

wars.name: Cuman wars in the Balkans and Hungary
wars.outcome: Cuman and Pecheneg raids on Adrianople (1078), the Balkans (1086, 1094-1095), Hungary (beaten by Ladislaus I in 1089; Coloman crushed in 1099), and help to the Asen and Peter uprising (1185) and Kaloyan at Adrianople (1205). No border of the confederation moved.

wars.name: Kipchak raids on Khwarezm, Volga Bulgaria and Qara Khitai
wars.outcome: The Kimaks sack Khwarezm in 1152 and 1197 and attack Volga Bulgaria in 1183; Kipchaks under Qara Ozan Khan attack Talas in 1181. No land changes hands on the pages.
wars.note: Qara Khitai page for the 1181 attack on Talas; the other dates are on the Kimek page.

wars.name: Mongol conquest of the Kipchak steppe

zones.text: the Volga-Don steppe west of the Urals
the Irtysh, Kazakh steppe and Aral steppe

wars.outcome: Subutai and Jebe chase the Merkit and Qangli Kipchak allies into northern Kazakhstan (1217 or 1218) without incorporating them; the Mongols defeat the Cumans in Subcaucasia (1220) and fight near the Kalka River (1223); in 1236 they defeat the eastern part of Cumania; the Cuman exodus into Bulgaria and Hungary follows (1237-1240); Köten is murdered in Pest in March 1241 and Cuman control of the Pontic steppes ends.
wars.note: Mongol invasion of Central Asia page for 1217-1218 and 1236; Cumans page for 1220-1241.

certainty.note: Nomad frontiers throughout: no page gives a line. The Cliopatria edges (Irtysh to the Don) are the best draw; the eastern end beyond Taraz and the western end at 38 E are doubtful (see keyframes).

notes: Start and end moved: Cliopatria's row runs 750-1235; the Kimek-Kipchak page dates the state 880-1035 (infobox) and the Cumans page ends Cuman control of the Pontic steppes in 1241. The first three shapes (750, 793, 850; 129 years) are marked wrong because the page has only a people (the Kimaks on the Irtysh) before the state formed at the end of the 9th century; a gap-filler could add the pre-state Kimaks and their Uyghur-held part. The row is kept as one confederation to 1241 (a 'rename' in 1055 to the Kipchak-Cuman names), because Cliopatria has one row and the pages give no break: the Kimek page's infobox ends in 1035 but the Cumans of 1055 are the same Kipchaks the Kimek page says migrated west from the 10th century. Cliopatria shape changes that no page dates (confidence 1): 896 (Ural-Turgay steppe), 1072 (south Urals and Middle Volga), 1147 (to Kara-Khitans), 1210 (to Khwarezm), 1220 and 1227 (to the Mongols); the 1056 step is page-backed (Oghuz lands, 1054-1055). The Mongol steps of 1220 and 1227 run about a decade before the pages' 1236. None of the pages gives an area (Kimek: none; Cumans: 'Danube to Taraz'; Golden Horde infobox 6 M km2 is for 1310), so the infobox comparison is impossible. Gaps and overlaps: (1) the Cumans page puts Cumania 'from the Danube in the west to Taraz in the east', but this row stops at 38 E and Cliopatria's 'Halych-Volhynia occupation' row (eu-16) holds 831-879 cells of the Dasht-i Kipchak region west of it in 1056-1240, so the Dnieper-Danube steppe is drawn as Galician-Volhynian occupation; the ia-01-g dossier 'cuman-kipchak-confederation' (Cliopatria 1056-1065, 315 km2 in Ukraine) and a gap-filler should draw it; (2) the eastern end of the shape (Altai, Upper Irtysh) conflicts with the Kimek page's statement that the Naiman displaced Kimaks and Kipchaks from the Mongolian Altai and Upper Irtysh in the 11th-12th centuries (undated); the Naiman have no dossier; (3) the Pechenegs (Pecheneg Khanates 889-1091) and the Torks have no dossier; (4) the 1237-1241 Cuman exodus to Hungary and Bulgaria is outside the shape. Matching events other dossiers should carry: oghuz-turks has the 1055 loss (this dossier gains in 1056); kara-khitans a gain of the middle Syr Darya in 1147; khwarezmid-empire a gain of the lower Syr Darya in 1210; mongol-empire gains in 1220, 1227 and 1241 (the Mongol dossier is ia-02). Counterparts needing dossiers: pechenegs, naiman, second-turkic-khaganate (not used here), kangar-union (via oghuz-turks). Names the gazetteer lacks: Imak (Imakia), Tamim (capitals only; not used in any region).
